purpose: The original half-step proxy passed, but this can reflect generic shrinkage rather than useful previous-step information. One additional CPU diagnostic distinguishes these mechanisms before paying for a controller implementation.
data: Same 400/100 calibration development groups; no new independent evidence and no benchmark answers.
fixed_control: Estimate one probability mean from all complete-step tokens in the 400 training questions. At each evaluated half-step use exactly the same previous-token count (min(previous complete step length,8)), but replace their probabilities with that fixed mean. The same current first-half tokens and second-half target are retained.
primary: Equal-question MSE on steps of 2..8 tokens in the 100 calibration validation questions.
advance_only_if: Previous-step pooling MSE is at least 5% lower than this fixed training-mean shrinkage control. Otherwise the claimed temporal-information advantage is unsupported and the temporal candidate is deferred without a GPU test or threshold search.
interpretation: This new specificity gate is explicitly a follow-up to the first CPU diagnostic, not a retrospectively claimed preregistration. Neither result estimates generated accuracy or compression.
